messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary deploy r2026 went green in CI but we're seeing a rising timeout/error wave in production. p95 ~ 400ms -> 1.9s; p99 from 900ms -> 4.8s. 5xx rate up from 0.2% -> 3.4%. Triggering page to SRE oncall @maria.nguyen and prod-eng lead @alice.prodeng

maria.nguyen: I'm on it. pulling up canary group logs & traces. assigning to samir for runtime traces.

kevin.liu: seeing errors are mostly upstream gateway timeouts (504) from task-exec service talking to runtime pool. stack traces point to increased kv-cache misses and longer model init tails.

samir.sre: confirming. continuous-batching latency distribution shifted — new kernel selection from deploy seems to cause per-token slowdowns on longer seqs. correlating with canary nodes only.

alice.prodeng: can we throttle canary or flip traffic back to previous revision? what's impact if we rollback?

maria.nguyen: impact: ~12% of user traffic served by canary group; estimated customer error surface ~3% of requests overall. several customer-reported timeouts hitting support.

kevin.liu: metrics:
```
before deploy:
 p95 380ms, p99 890ms, 5xx 0.2%
after canary: (canary nodes)
 p95 1.9s, p99 4.8s, 5xx 3.4%
```

samir.sre: traces show cold KV cache for some shards + a fallback path that does a synchronous quantize call on first request. that path used to be async in previous runtime. suspect kernel selector logic change in r2026.

alice.prodeng: can we quick-fix config to disable new kernel selection on canary? otherwise we should rollback. timeboxed decision in 10m.

maria.nguyen: rolling canary traffic down to 0% now. executing rollback plan with deploy-bot. @deploy-bot please run rollback for service/runtime-compiler -> previous stable
deploy-bot: command received: rollback service/runtime-compiler to r2025. initiating. :gear:

oncall-bot: (system) Pager acknowledged by maria.nguyen at 2213456792

kevin.liu: looks like traffic is shifting off canary. p95 dropping: 1.9s -> 540ms and p99 -> 1.1s within 45s. 5xx back under 0.6%.

maria.nguyen: rollback complete according to deploy logs. validating health checks and tracing.

samir.sre: verifying KV cache warmup on rolled-back nodes — warmup completes, fallback sync path not hit anymore. traces look normal.

alice.prodeng: pushing status update to support and status page. draft: "We detected an increase in timeouts after a canary deploy earlier today; we've reverted the deployment and are monitoring — no further customer impact expected." @status-bot please post when confirmed.

status-bot: prepared status draft, awaiting approval.

kevin.liu: runbook check: no other services altered. network metrics normal. allocating a followup action: disable the new kernel-selection flag in staging and run long tail-load tests.

maria.nguyen: handing off to followup: samir + alice to run regression analysis and root cause. I'll close the page once followup ticket is created.

samir.sre: creating ticket INF-5421 with logs, trace ids, and reproducer steps. assigning to runtime-team. blocked on repro for shorter seqs.

alice.prodeng: note for postmortem: include quantitative customer impact (support tickets, error windows), canary config (traffic %), and why rollout allowed this kernel selection change without extended e2e tail tests.

maria.nguyen: post-incident checklist:
- rollback completed (2213457010)
- mitigation validated (2213457045)
- followup ticket created INF-5421
- status update queued

kevin.liu: thumbs up. also suggest temporary guardrail: add automated p99 smoke check that blocks kernel-selection changes for canary if p99 increases > 2x baseline.

status-bot: status update posted to status.redwood.ai at 2213457098

maria.nguyen: closing page and unpaging. leaving thread for followup actions. thanks everyone for fast coordination. :thumbsup:
